why: The update contract needs evidence before implementation, and it must stay separate from PR 1540

decision: Treat an exact old template tree as the minimum update state
why: A changelog or version label cannot distinguish an upstream change from a user edit without the old bytes and Git mode
evidence: Copier and Cruft update algorithms; exhaustive B/C/U state table

decision: Use the generated app root commit as the first-update base
why: Samebase has seeded one parentless commit containing the complete starter tree since 2026-02-13

decision: Keep the current launcher SHA headers but do not call them template versions
why: The SHA proves that three launcher bodies form one synchronized group. It does not identify an upstream release or local edits.

decision: Do not generalize manual v<N> comments to all template scripts
why: The old prototype covered 15 TypeScript scripts, while the tracked starter has 99 files and eight public exports from v1912 through v1983 touched 29 paths. Only 11 were TypeScript files under scripts. Comments also miss deletes, renames, modes, JSON, and user edits.

decision: Keep the canonical changelog in the public Samebase plugin
why: The plugin is public and agent-owned. A changelog copied into each generated app becomes stale at creation time.

decision: Put one stable public changelog link in each starter instead of copying the changelog
why: A copied changelog stops being current after the next starter change. A stable link lets an agent read the current record.
evidence: Current starter AGENTS.md and public plugin layout

decision: After a complete update, store only the exact accepted public starter commit in .samebase/template.json
why: The public commit supplies the complete old tree for the next three-way merge. Extra time, URL, path, and hash fields duplicate Git or widen trust.
evidence: B/C/U model; Cruft; Copier; independent contract review

decision: Ship public guidance before update code
why: The changelog is useful by itself. Real temporary-repository trials must show repeated work before Samebase adds a planner or writer.

decision: Use a generated app root as the first base only after its complete tree matches a documented public starter commit at v1912 or later
why: A first commit is evidence only when Samebase can positively identify its bytes. Older and altered roots stay on the manual path.
evidence: Current seed history; public exports v1912 through v1983; independent contract review

decision: Use native git merge-tree with an explicit base instead of implementing the B/C/U table in TypeScript
why: Git already handles bytes, executable flags, absence, and conflicts. A local unrelated-history trial returned the exact v1983 tree.
evidence: https://git-scm.com/docs/git-merge-tree; local v1982 to v1983 trial
